definition: In mathematics, mirror descent is an iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function.
details: It generalizes algorithms such as gradient descent and multiplicative weights.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Mirror descent — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
